topic.title: Protocols: MCP, A2A & OpenTelemetry
topic.slideRef: M3L1 Slides 31–32; M3L4 Slide 20; M3L5 Slides 8–10
topic.summary: MCP (agent ↔ tools/data) vs A2A (agent ↔ agent), HTTP + JSON-RPC 2.0 + SSE, RFC 8615 /.well-known/agent-card.json, MCP Toolbox for DBs (<10 LoC), OTel gen_ai.* & SPAN < TRACE < SESSION < TASK.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols (Swapped-Definition Trap) | Trigger #16 | M3L1 Slide 31
questions.q: What is the fundamental architectural difference between Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A)?
options: MCP connects an agent to its tools, APIs, and data sources; A2A enables independent agents to discover each other and collaborate as peers
A2A connects an agent to databases and tools; MCP enables peer-to-peer delegation between autonomous agents
MCP is only for on-premises servers, while A2A is only for BigQuery SQL queries
MCP and A2A are identical protocols with different marketing names
questions.why: Watch out for the classic swapped-definition trap (§1.6): MCP = agent ↔ tools, APIs, and data sources. A2A = agent ↔ agent (peer discovery and collaboration to delegate work).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols | Self-Test #8 & Trigger #16 | M3L1 Slide 31
questions.q: Which three core web technologies is the A2A protocol built on?
options: HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, and Server-Sent Events (SSE)
WebSockets, GraphQL, and WebRTC
MQTT, Protobuf binary framing, and FTP
SOAP XML, CORBA, and Raw TCP sockets
questions.why: Per Self-Test #8 and §1.6: A2A reuses existing web standards—specifically HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0, and Server-Sent Events (SSE). Avoid exotic stack distractors like WebSockets/GraphQL/WebRTC or MQTT.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols | Self-Test #8 & Trigger #16 | M3L1 Slide 32
questions.q: Where is an A2A Agent Card hosted according to the RFC 8615 well-known URI standard?
options: https://{server_domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json (older versions used /.well-known/agent.json)
https://{server_domain}/api/v1/skills/SKILL.md
~/.gemini/config/skills/agent-card.yaml
urn:agent:google:agent-card
questions.why: Per §1.6 & Self-Test #8: An A2A Agent Card is published at https://{server_domain}/.well-known/agent-card.json following RFC 8615 well-known URIs (older versions used /.well-known/agent.json).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols | Trigger #20 | M3L4 Slide 20
questions.q: What does Google's open-source MCP Toolbox for Databases handle for developers out of the box?
options: Connection pooling, authentication (IAM), and OpenTelemetry observability, allowing database tools to be added to an agent in under 10 lines of code
Training custom foundation models directly inside Cloud SQL stored procedures
Replacing Agent Registry with a local SQLite catalog
Converting Python agents into Java servlets
questions.why: Per §1.6 & Trigger #20: MCP Toolbox for Databases is Google's open-source MCP server for databases that handles connection pooling, IAM authentication, and observability so you can add DB tools in under 10 lines of code.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 Protocols | Tab 3 M1L4
questions.q: What enterprise capabilities do Google-managed MCP servers layer on top of standard open-source MCP?
options: MCP discovery (via Agent Registry), IAM and VPC Service Controls governance, spec-compliant auth, Model Armor scanning, and tracing/audit-log observability
Unlimited free Gemini Pro token usage with no IAM checks
Automatic removal of all system prompts to save context tokens
Direct bypass of VPC Service Controls perimeters
questions.why: Per §1.6: Google-managed MCP servers add MCP discovery (via Agent Registry), IAM and VPC Service Controls governance, spec-compliant authentication, Model Armor scanning, and tracing/audit-log observability.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 & §6.1 OpenTelemetry | Trigger #21 | M3L5 Slide 8
questions.q: What is the purpose of OpenTelemetry's 'gen_ai.*' semantic conventions in multi-agent systems?
options: They standardize both attribute names and semantic meanings across libraries, languages, and providers, enabling consistent cross-vendor observability
They only standardize attribute names while leaving the meaning up to each vendor
They encrypt model weights stored in Cloud Storage
They replaceSessionService in ADK 2.0
questions.why: Per §1.6 & Trigger #21: OpenTelemetry 'gen_ai.*' attributes make GenAI telemetry mean the same thing (both names and meanings) across libraries, languages, and model providers. Watch out for the trap 'OTel only standardizes names, not meanings.'

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §6.1 OTel 4-Level Hierarchy | Trigger #21 | M3L5 Slides 8–10
questions.q: What is the correct 4-level OpenTelemetry GenAI observability hierarchy ordered from SMALLEST to LARGEST?
options: 1. SPAN (atomic call) < 2. TRACE (single turn) < 3. SESSION (multi-turn conversation) < 4. TASK (multi-agent workflow)
1. TRACE < 2. SPAN < 3. TASK < 4. SESSION
1. SESSION < 2. TRACE < 3. SPAN < 4. TASK
1. TASK < 2. SESSION < 3. TRACE < 4. SPAN
questions.why: Per §6.1 & Trigger #21 (M3L5 Slides 8–10): Smallest to largest is: 1. SPAN (1 atomic LLM/tool/agent call) < 2. TRACE (1 end-to-end user turn) < 3. SESSION (multi-turn conversation) < 4. TASK (background workflow across agents/sessions, proposed).

questions.q: An enterprise wants multiple teams' agents (built in different frameworks) to share standardized access to internal CRM and ERP tools without rewriting tool adapters for every agent. What should they adopt?
options: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers registered in Agent Registry
Inline Python FunctionTools copied and pasted into each team's codebase
Setting output_schema on every agent
Basic Sensitive Data Protection templates
questions.why: MCP provides a universal open protocol connecting agents to shared tools, APIs, and data sources so tools are built once on an MCP server and reused across any MCP-compatible agent.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.6 & Tab 2 M3L1 Slides 31–32
questions.q: Why does the A2A protocol include Server-Sent Events (SSE) alongside HTTP and JSON-RPC 2.0?
options: To stream real-time task status updates and partial artifacts during long-running asynchronous agent-to-agent delegations
Because JSON-RPC 2.0 cannot transmit text strings over HTTP
To compile Python functions into WebAssembly in the browser
To bypass Agent Gateway TLS inspection
questions.why: Peer agents often perform long-running, multi-step tasks; A2A uses Server-Sent Events (SSE) over HTTP to stream asynchronous progress updates and artifacts back to the calling agent.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §6.1 OpenTelemetry | M3L5 Slide 8
questions.q: In OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, how are a Trace and its Spans structurally related during a single user-to-agent turn?
options: A Trace represents the full end-to-end turn as a tree, where each Span is a node representing an atomic operation (e.g., an LLM call or tool execution)
A Span contains multiple Traces across different users
A Trace only logs billing costs, while a Span only logs HTTP errors
Traces and Spans are unrelated flat log files
questions.why: Per §6.1: A Trace captures a single end-to-end user-to-agent turn as a tree structure, and Spans are the individual nodes representing each atomic operation (agent invocation, LLM call, or tool call).
